gaps.gap: The inverted-flux (2-f) null is read as the false-alarm rate of the whole screen ('roughly one in five first-screen passes is noise or a systematic', 'false-alarm rate measured rather than guessed'). Re-derived from runs/poolA_main/triage_all.csv by best-peak period: P 0.5-2 d real 24 vs inverted 25; 2-10 d 33 vs 36; 10-20 d 12 vs 4; 20-40 d 369 vs 30. So (a) below 10 d the stage-1 screen has zero discriminating power (real = inverted), exactly where kic-009520080 (2.38 d) and kic-001577049 (0.54 d) live; (b) the 12x excess at 20-40 d is the Kepler downlink/quarter-edge regime whose dips are sign-asymmetric (upward-only clipping in prepare(), SPSDs, thermal settling) and cannot be mimicked by 2-f. The null calibrates sign-symmetric noise and variability only. It is also biased low: the inverted best BLS peak is a 7-h box at P < 1 d in 5,841/6,365 stars (median P 0.62 d, dur 7.05 h) and is killed by the duty-cycle cut, whereas only 2,902/6,365 real best peaks are; the best *allowed* inverted peak is never evaluated.
gaps.why_it_matters: The headline calibration claim of the whole project rests on this comparison; a referee will reject the 'one in five' statement and the 'measured false-alarm rate' phrasing immediately, and the asymmetry means the real-pass excess at long periods is systematics, not evidence.
gaps.fix: Text: in docs/10 L17 and L48, the triage.md header and prereg L54 replace with 'the inverted run bounds the sign-symmetric noise/variability pass rate; it does not model dip-shaped systematics. Real vs inverted passes per period bin: 24/25, 33/36, 12/4, 369/30.' Code: in bls_one() mask res.power where duration/period > max_duty_cycle before argmax (both polarities), register as prereg v1.3 and label the re-triage post-hoc; have triage.py print the per-period-bin table; add a second null that targets systematics (same screen on light curves with quarters/months shuffled in time, or injected synthetic gap-edge ramps).

gaps.gap: Weakest link in the pixel argument: the target sits at or outside the stamp edge in most quarters (within 0.5 px of an edge or outside: 006699887 7/13 quarters, 009520080 12/17, 010213563 13/13; e.g. target_px x = -0.1/-0.2). The deficit centroid is built only from in-stamp pixels with SNR > 2 (typically 2-4 pixels), so it is pinned to the edge column, i.e. onto the target, and no uncertainty is attached to target_to_deficit_arcsec (1.1-2.3 arcsec claimed on 3.98-arcsec pixels at peak SNR 5-7). The 'closer to target than any other source' vote compares only Gaia sources whose pixel position is inside the stamp (in_stamp), so any source beyond the edge is never a competitor. The Gaussian sigma = 0.9 px is not the Kepler PRF (disclosed) and the best model still has summed chi2 839 over ~374 pixels for 009520080 (reduced ~2.2). Meanwhile the genuinely strong evidence computed per quarter (chi2_gauss_at_source for each neighbour) is never summarised: Gaussian at target vs at the brightest in-stamp neighbour sums to 536 vs 1047 (G 15.1) for 006699887, 839 vs 1568 (G 14.8) for 009520080, 1143 vs 1556 (G 14.3) for 010213563. The positive-control validation (one star, 13/13) had no negative control.
gaps.why_it_matters: The three 'on target' verdicts are the basis for 'close to a candidate'; as written the quantitative test cannot exclude an off-stamp blend, and the test has never been shown to reject anything real.
gaps.fix: Code: (1) skip or flag quarters where the target is < 0.5 px from a stamp edge; (2) bootstrap the centroid over events (or over the 24 random-phase maps) to get an error on target_to_deficit_arcsec and report an offset significance; (3) include Gaia sources up to 2 px outside the stamp as candidate positions with edge-truncated Gaussian models; (4) add a dilution/consistency check: expected missing light = depth x median KBONUS PSF FLUX (e/s) vs fitted amp_gauss_at_target x 2*pi*sigma^2; (5) put per-neighbour delta-chi2 and 'quarters neighbour wins' into summary and docs/10. Controls: run pixel_vet on the 15 SAME_TPF known FP/EB survivors in runs/poolA_main/survivors.csv (e.g. kic-009156588, KOI false positive on the same TPF) as negative controls before trusting any 'on target'. gaps.gap: Two stage-2 statistics are ill-defined or inconsistent with stage 1. (1) tls_sde_min = 9.0 is applied to a TLS periodogram computed over +/-2 % of the known period; SDE = (max - median)/std is only meaningful for a full-range search, so in a narrow window it is arbitrary, yet it is the single biggest stage-2 killer (349 of 438 fail on tls_sde). (2) tls_snr is TLS's white-noise formal SNR, the kind of statistic stage 1 deliberately replaced with the empirical box noise; stage 2 has no empirical-SNR floor at all, so kic-001577049 'survives' with snr_emp_pass2 = 1.88 (box_noise 703 ppm, depth 1324 ppm) because tls_snr = 18.5. docs/10 prints SNR 1.9 for a stage-2 survivor without comment; a newcomer reads it as an error.
gaps.why_it_matters: The survivor count of 11 is governed by a statistic with no defined null distribution, and a 1.9-sigma signal is carried as a survivor; a referee will ask why the stage-1 SNR floor disappears at stage 2.
gaps.fix: Replace tls_sde in the narrow window with a full-range TLS SDE (or drop the criterion and rely on snr); add snr_emp_pass2 >= 7.1 to stage2_vetting, labelled post-hoc with a revision_log entry, and recount (kic-001577049 drops). At minimum, footnote in docs/10 that stage 2 has no snr_emp cut by registration, the signal passes on TLS formal SNR, and any added cut is post-hoc. State explicitly in docs/10 which TLS quantities are formal.

runnability: Merged from both audits (this pass was read-only: nothing in the repo was modified, no pipeline stage executed; the dedup map is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-ZyushgPlanet/0a31cad6-114a-5cca-8219-924182316e90/scratchpad/critic-merge/dedup_map.md). In the existing .venv every README/CLAUDE.md entry point parses: `python -m pipeline.run_batch --help`, `pipeline.triage --help`, `pipeline.vet_batch --help`, `pipeline.modal_client --help`, `pipeline.run --help`, plus `pipeline.pixel_vet --help` and `pipeline.ephemeris_match` (self-test prints the Kepler-169 e match). On a fresh clone the README quick-start works for `run_batch` (data re-downloaded from MAST) but `python -m pipeline.triage --run-id pilot` fails because triage imports ephemeris_match, which reads four CSVs under gitignored data/known/ that no script or doc downloads. For the Modal run, `pipeline.triage --run-id poolA_main` as written in CLAUDE.md fails (verified: FileNotFoundError runs/poolA_main/config_used.json; needs `--config pipeline/prereg_poolA.json`); triage was in fact run against the live prereg file (config_sha ccca76e8 in results.jsonl equals the current file minus stage2_vetting). `pipeline.modal_client` needs a gitignored .modal_endpoints.json and the `modal` package is neither in requirements.txt nor installed, so the Modal batch is not reproducible from the docs. Pixel localisation is reachable only via scripts/pixel_vet_survivors.py, which no document mentions. Target-list SHA-256 matches prereg (27052817...); pilot = ranks 1-100, Modal = 101-6465 as README states. All referee-lens numbers were re-derived with short pandas/json scripts from runs/poolA_main/{triage_all.csv,survivors.csv,vet_summary.csv}, the vet.json/pixel.json pairs for kic-006699887, kic-009520080, kic-010213563, kic-010213563, kic-001577049 and kic-006448637, runs/poolA_pilot and runs/controls outputs, and the git history of pipeline/prereg_poolA.json and pipeline/*.py; every stated number in docs/10 §2 traced correctly to its file.
overall: Two audits with complementary lenses (newcomer/reproducibility and sceptical referee) merged into 28 gaps (6 blocking, 12 important, 10 minor) and 15 contradictions; four pairs were duplicates (Kepler-138 control claim, 438/95 vs pool size, prereg name v1.1, kic-001577049 SNR 1.9) and one item split (config_used.json into the triage-command blocker, the 12/13 vs 13/13 docstring kept separately). Agreement between the audits: the quantitative core transcribes correctly (every docs/10 §2 number for the 11 survivors, the 11 pixel summaries, the KIC 5689121 13/13 control, 438/95, 125 s/star, rank ranges and target hash trace to runs/poolA_main, runs/controls and prereg_poolA.json), and the bookkeeping (frozen list, hashed config, per-criterion reporting, controls kept) is better than most agent-run searches. The blocking problems are in inference, registration discipline and reproducibility, not transcription: (1) the inverted null is over-read as a false-alarm rate when per period bin real and inverted passes are equal below 10 d (24/25, 33/36) and differ 12x only in the 20-40 d gap-systematics regime that sign inversion cannot mimic, and it evaluates the inverted star's disallowed best peak; (2) a stage-2 criterion was relaxed after the control failed the registered version with no revision_log entry, the version string lags the log, and registration timestamps post-date their commits; (3) the pixel argument has the target on the stamp edge in most quarters, a centroid with no error bar built from 2-4 pixels, in-stamp-only competitors, no negative control, an untested noise fallback and post-hoc disposition categories, while the strong per-neighbour delta-chi2 evidence that exists is never reported and one 'off target' is really 'not testable'; (4) stage 2 applies TLS SDE in a +/-2 % window where it is undefined (the largest killer), has no empirical-SNR floor (a 1.9-sigma signal survives), is blind to a -4-sigma phase-0.5 brightening by a one-sided test, and never applies the per-quartile test it claims; (5) a fresh clone cannot run triage (gitignored data/known/ with no downloader) and the CLAUDE.md triage command fails on Modal runs. Important follow-ons are the unsupported Kepler-138 stage-2/pixel claim, pass counts quoted on the 6,365-star subset against a 6,465 pool, 'planet candidate' before TRICERATOPS, the overclaim phrases ('firmly', 'validated', 'never-searched', 'every change made before pool stars were judged'), run.py wrongly named for pixel work, undocumented Modal deployment, and docs/05 §8 / docs/08 prescribing artefacts never built. Fixes are mostly a few lines of text and small code additions (duty-cycle-aware peak selection, centroid bootstrap, off-stamp competitors, deficit-vs-expected-flux check, noise-method logging, stage-2 SNR floor, two-sided secondary flag, config_used.json on fetch, a fetch_known.py), plus one afternoon of negative-control pixel runs on the 15 known same-TPF false positives already in survivors.csv; none changes a scientific result, but several change what the repo may claim.
